item.description: arXiv:2606.22598v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A holographic code assigns a state-dependent entropy remainder to every boundary region, but such remainders need not be the extremal lengths of any one bulk metric. We study this common-source question for the proto-area of a calibrated recovery, the entropy of a boundary region minus that of the matter recovered from it. At zeroth order the reference values must match the lengths of one reference geometry in a fixed renormalization scheme, and this matching also determines the entropy-to-length factor. On a graph with a fixed minimum-cut chamber the data derivatives must lie in the image of the cut-incidence matrix, whose left null vectors are witnesses. On the hyperbolic disk the first variation of renormalized length is the rank-two geodesic X-ray transform, with closed range in an adapted data space, and the geodesic displacement, fixed by a forced Jacobi equation, enters at second order. The resulting normal Hessian gives a gauge-invariant criterion, necessary and sufficient, for a regular pair of response coefficients to come from one metric two-jet. For the constant-curvature family generated by a boundary reparametrization the Hessian has a nonzero rank-four mode, so the image of the length map is curved. For a fixed recovery the proto-area Hessian is minus the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori information lost in recovery, which the Petz map decomposes orthogonally at a product reference, and which, on a finite-dimensional space of logical directions with positive minimum retained fraction, is at most a sharp multiple of the retained information. Geometric realization requires this loss to reproduce the normal length Hessian on every interval. Two codes show that exact regional area operators can fail to sew into one graph geometry, and that a matched reference with vanishing first response can fail at second order. All criteria refer to one recovery branch and one extremal-surface branch.
item.dc:creator: Ruiliang Li

item.title: Exact and Finite de Sitter QFT from CFT
item.description: arXiv:2606.24382v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parallel to the AdS Scale-Space construction in \cite{Yang:2026AdS}, we construct a $(d+1)$-dimensional de Sitter QFT directly from $d$-dimensional CFT data. The dS geometry is the moduli space of oriented balls, and the lifted operators are obtained by conformal-family Casimir completion. The Euclidean parent CFT gives a finite wavefunction representation, while the Minkowski parent CFT gives a double-time representation that is unitary in the parent-time polarization. This provides a CFT-based framework for reexamining puzzles of dS and double-time QFT.
item.dc:creator: Haitang Yang

item.title: Gravitational wave scattering at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$: Murua construction and elliptics
item.description: arXiv:2606.27544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the amplitude for the scattering of a gravitational wave off of a spinless point particle at fourth order in Newton's constant, using the worldline quantum field theory formalism. A decomposition of our master integrals incorporating Murua coefficients allows us to entirely bypass the cut subtraction needed to convert the scattering amplitude into the Magnusian, the latter mapping directly onto the scattering phase shift in partial wave space. Elliptic functions appear in momentum space for the first time for this process at this order. To compare to the phase shift from black hole perturbation theory, we present an analytical method for performing the partial wave projection of the new elliptic sector to any partial wave order $\ell$, and verify the equivalence of the Magnusian and the phase shift. This demonstrates that point-particle worldline quantum field theory accurately describes Schwarzschild black holes up to $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$.
item.dc:creator: Yilber Fabian Bautista, Mathias Driesse, Kays Haddad, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen

item.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.03679v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature. We explicitly relate HR to Topological Regularisation (TR), where the latter prescribes to add the Euler term to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian density, with a precise coefficient so as to ensure that the resulting density is polynomial in the anti de Sitter (AdS) curvature. The polynomial is still asymptotically divergent. We find that the aforementioned, unique conformal gravity action in 8D, reproduces the polynomial, together with extra boundary terms that cancel the divergent terms in the action. We conjecture that, in arbitrary even dimension, HR is equivalent to conformally completing the Einstein-Hilbert action with negative cosmological constant, plus the Euler term with fixed coupling prescribed by TR.
item.dc:creator: Giorgos Anastasiou, Ignacio J. Araya, Nicolas Boulanger, Rodrigo Olea, Davide Rovere

item.title: A Horizon-to-Boundary Dictionary Linking Smooth Horizon Continuation, Pole-Skipping, and $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ Lowest-Weight Structure
item.description: arXiv:2607.03800v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study pole-skipping for a scalar field in the JT/AdS$_2$ black-hole background. Previous work established the local mechanism: at a pole-skipping point, a near-horizon recurrence relation becomes degenerate and an additional regular expansion coefficient is left undetermined. We take this local degeneracy as the starting point and track two independent solutions normalized at the AdS boundary, denoted by $R_1$ and $R_2$ for the source and response branches, respectively. Let $\widehat A$ and $\widehat B$ denote the source and response coefficients after their common singular factor is removed, and let $\chi_\mu$ denote the universal ingoing horizon factor. We find \[ \widehat A=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_2}{\chi_\mu}\in C^\infty, \qquad \widehat B=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_1}{\chi_\mu}\in C^\infty . \] Thus the source and response zeros correspond separately to horizon smoothness of the two boundary-normalized solutions after the ingoing factor is removed. At integer resonance the local regular solution contains an additional coefficient $a_N$. In the JT/AdS$_2$ model, continuation of the nonresonant ingoing solution fixes $a_N=0$ and thereby selects a unique retarded value at resonance, although unrestricted approaches in parameter space remain path dependent. At the endpoint of the pole-skipping lattice, the response branch is a lowest-weight state of the background $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry. A static holographic-superconductor example further shows that simultaneous horizon smoothness is insufficient if the two boundary branches are linearly dependent. A two-branch pole-zero intersection therefore requires \[ W[R_1,R_2]\neq0. \] These results distinguish the known local horizon degeneracy from the global relation between boundary branches and the resonant horizon solution space.
item.dc:creator: Yoon-Seok Choun, Ki-Seok Kim

item.title: No off-diagonal quantum focusing for R\'enyi divergences
item.description: arXiv:2607.07799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) is a mathematical expression of the idea that semiclassical gravity remains universally attractive. In its non-gravitational limit, the diagonal inequality is the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), which requires convexity of relative entropy with respect to the vacuum under null deformations. R\'enyi divergences generalize relative entropy, and positive results for the diagonal R\'enyi QNEC raise the question of whether they also satisfy the off-diagonal inequalities required by a full focusing principle. We show that classical correlations between distinct null generators obstruct this extension for any non-affine R\'enyi-type divergence satisfying data processing, tensor additivity, and matched classical-quantum conditioning.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

item.title: Relative entropy for $\lambda \phi^4$ in the Rindler wedge
item.description: arXiv:2607.07810v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the relative entropy between the vacuum and a coherent state in the Rindler wedge for an interacting $\lambda \phi^4$ theory to first order in $\lambda$. We construct the perturbatively interacting Weyl algebra of the wedge, and employ Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and the Araki-Uhlmann formula to compute the relative entropy. We verify that the relative entropy reduces to the classical (interacting) boost Noether charge, analogously to the free theory, and that the Bekenstein bound holds.
item.dc:creator: Markus B. Fr\"ob, Albert Much, Kyriakos Papadopoulos

item.title: Decoupling Limit of Quiver Theories and the Angular Spectra of Extreme C-metrics
item.description: arXiv:2607.08747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the angular eigenvalue problem of the extreme charged C-metric. Starting from a constrained five-point Fuchsian description of the non-extremal angular equation, we obtain its extreme limit by decoupling a hypermultiplet in the dual four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$, $\mathrm{SU(2)}\times \mathrm{SU(2)}$ linear quiver gauge theory. We derive the parameter dictionary and renormalized Matone relations, and connect the physical limit $Q\to M$ to the quiver decoupling by an explicit coordinate transformation. Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Peng Yang, Kilar Zhang

item.title: The Information Content of Krylov Observables: A Machine Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2607.17346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We employ machine learning techniques to estimate the amount of information contained in three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity $C(t)$, the discrete Wigner negativity $N(t)$, and the normalized negativity $\chi(t)=N(t)/|S(t)|$, where $S(t)$ is the survival amplitude. We study thermofield-double evolutions on GUE, GOE and Poisson spectra, and on the integrable $SL(2,R)$ Krylov chain of a two-dimensional CFT primary, with Lanczos coefficients $b_n=\alpha\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$. To introduce chaos we add a GUE random matrix to the integrable chain, $H(\varepsilon)=H_{SL(2,R)}+\varepsilon R_0 W_{GUE}$, where $R_0$ is its spectral half-width. Either $C(t)$ or $N(t)$ alone determines the thermofield temperature, with $R^2\simeq0.999$. However, neither can reconstruct the fine structure of the spectral form factor. In the integrable sector all three observables carry the same information. When we turn on chaos an asymmetry appears: $\chi$ predicts $C$ better than $C$ predicts $\chi$. This gap grows from $+0.33$ to $+0.77$, while the same gap for the raw negativity decays to zero. The extra information comes from the survival amplitude, and $\chi(t)$ carries it while $C(t)$ can still be recovered from $\chi(t)$. We derive a lower bound on this gap, set by the fraction of the variance of $\chi$ that comes from $S$.
item.dc:creator: Ritam Basu

item.title: Conformal symmetry, SM and Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.22354v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is a bottom up attempt to incorporate the standard model and general relativity in a unique quantum field theory. The tentative model presented here in particular is free of chiral gauge and gravitational anomalies that appear in the divergence of currents, and in the divergence and trace of the energy-momentum tensor when the SM matter couples to gravity. The fermion spectrum is composed of two multiplets, the SM (left) multiplet and a mirror copy (right) with opposite handedness. The right multiplet is interpreted as describing the dark matter world. The natural symmetry of the theory is enlarged to incorporate also Weyl invariance, by introducing one or more dilaton fields. After the cosmological and theoretical motivations, the necessary formalism is introduced for algebraic renormalization: gauge fixings, ghosts, propagators and vertices and their interplay in guaranteeing the conditions for convergence of the subtracted amplitudes according to the BPHZL scheme, the Slavnov-Taylor identity and the relevant enlarged BRST symmetry. The corresponding (conformal) cohomology is analyzed and found to be trivial: there are no non-trivial even trace anomalies in theories with dilatons, but there are plenty of trivial ones, which require corresponding counterterms in the effective action. It is shown that such counterterms can play an important role in freeing the theory of unphysical particles.
item.dc:creator: Loriano Bonora

item.title: Infrared Problem in Quantum Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.00204v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that the inclusive cross section in QED is infrared finite. In the standard diagram techniques this result follows from cancellation of infrared divergences. We suggest a new approach that should lead to IR -safe computational technique for QED with massive fermions.
item.dc:creator: Igor Frolov, Albert Schwarz

item.title: Local subtractions and renormalization-group monotonicity: exact defect and sphere flows
item.description: arXiv:2608.02447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We ask when the sphere free energy of a quantum field theory, after subtraction of its local counterterms in a fixed renormalization prescription, decreases monotonically along the renormalization-group (RG) flow. The counterterms fix the required zeros of the subtraction polynomial, but positivity of the spectral data alone does not determine monotonicity. For Gaussian determinants, complete monotonicity of a rescaled integrated heat trace is sufficient. This condition proves monotonicity for Robin boundary flows on every sphere $S^p$, $p\ge2$. A related identity proves monotonicity for massive Dirac fields on odd spheres $S^d$, $d\ge3$. Conversely, under the stated endpoint and decay assumptions, an approach to the infrared value from below excludes every endpoint-preserving finite polynomial subtraction. For the double-trace families considered here, driven by $\mathcal O^2$ on spherical surface defects and, at leading order in large $N$, on $S^3$, a monotone subtraction exists exactly when the dimension of $\mathcal O$ is at least $1/2$ and $(3-\sqrt{37/13})/2$, respectively. Below these thresholds no subtraction is monotone, although the spectra remain positive. The same determinants describe double-trace boundary flows of a free massive scalar in AdS$_3$ and AdS$_4$, where the classifications carry over. Finally, with contact terms fixed, the leading infrared sphere coefficient of a flow from a three-dimensional conformal field theory to a gapped phase is proportional to a difference of nonnegative stress-tensor spectral moments. In the massive critical $O(N)$ model this difference vanishes at leading order and is negative at order $N^0$.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Scardino

item.title: An explicit four-corner dictionary for (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.08669v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity admits four algebraic descriptions interrelated by dualities. On the Frobenius manifold (FM) side the theory is built either on the $A_{1}$ manifold of $Q(y)=y^{2}+u_{1}$ ($y$-side) or on the $A_{p-1}$ manifold in the variable $x$ ($x$-side). On the spectral curve / topological recursion (SC) side the analogous choice is the Chebyshev curve and its $x\leftrightarrow y$ swap. FM-$y$, SC-$y$ require a resonance transformation between the KdV times and the Liouville couplings, while the other two do not. We work out the explicit correspondence between the four approaches at the level of the dispersionless tau-function. The normalisation-independent three-point ratios agree with conformal field theory in all four formulations, and matching the full amplitudes fixes a single per-insertion factor reproducing the signed Verlinde matrices. We use the Kharchev--Marshakov integral transform of the basis functions, whose determinant gives an explicit relation between the corresponding tau-functions and realises the $x\!\leftrightarrow\! y$ swap at genus zero. Once the independently fixed linear SC-$x$ normalisation is imposed, the Laurent deformation in the second coordinate gives an alternative genus-zero derivation of the known compact resonance transformation for the whole (2,p) series, including all mixed coefficients.
item.dc:creator: A. Alexandrov, V. Belavin

item.title: Holographic multipartite entanglement dynamics in AdS$_3$-Vaidya
item.description: arXiv:2608.09304v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how multipartite entanglement is dynamically reorganized during holographic thermalization following a global quench in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$. We first use the $n$-partite information $(-1)^n I_n$ to probe collective multipartite entanglement in holographic configurations where the full $n$-region entanglement wedge is connected while all fewer-party ones are disconnected, thereby excluding fewer-party contributions. The spatial range of multipartite entanglement first expands and then contracts as the system approaches its late-time locally thermal state. Entanglement involving different numbers of parties develops on comparable early-time scales, while the entanglement that involves more parties relaxes more slowly, revealing a transient propagation from shorter to longer spatial distances. We further compute the Markov gap and the genuine tripartite multi-entropy as complementary probes of tripartite entanglement. The Markov gap can remain enhanced after local thermalization, whereas the genuine tripartite multi-entropy undergoes a nonmonotonic evolution and returns to its vacuum value for the adjacent tripartition considered in this work. These results show that a global quench redistributes the entanglement across spatial scales and reorganizes its multipartite structure.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Xiang Ju, Ya-Wen Sun, Yang Zhao, Hao-Ran Zhou

item.title: Holographic Complexity as a Probe of Boundary Entropy in AdS/BCFT
item.description: arXiv:2608.10348v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how the sewing operations familiar from topological quantum field theory provide a useful organizational framework for semiclassical AdS/BCFT path integrals. Our purpose is not to identify AdS/BCFT with a topological field theory: the bulk geometry, the end-of-the-world brane, and the on-shell action remain intrinsically metric-dependent. Rather, we use the TQFT language of state preparation, orientation reversal, and gluing to separate interface data from local geometric contributions. For AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$, we review how the Euclidean on-shell action and the Ryu--Takayanagi prescription reproduce the Affleck--Ludwig boundary entropy $\log g$ after holographic renormalization. We then formulate the Complexity=Action calculation in the presence of an end-of-the-world brane, carefully distinguishing bulk, brane, joint, and null-boundary contributions. We emphasize that finite terms in a relative Wheeler--DeWitt action depend on the choice of regulator matching and on the null-boundary counterterm scheme unless their scheme independence is established explicitly. Finally, we extend the geometric construction to a planar BTZ background and derive the brane embedding from the Neumann boundary condition. The resulting framework clarifies which aspects of holographic complexity are sensitive to boundary conditions and which require further renormalization input before they can be interpreted as universal boundary data.
item.dc:creator: Fabiano F. Santos

item.title: Exact Evaluation of Lattice-Regularized Scalar Field Vacuum Amplitude via Site Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2608.13117v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A novel approach to a computation of vacuum amplitude for a single scalar field in any number of dimensions with arbitrary potential on a lattice is proposed. The computation involves symmetrization of kinetic exponential factor in the path integral over all permutations of lattice sites and Waring decomposition of the symmetrized expression.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Asnin

item.title: Gravitational wave signatures from area metric gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.16046v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Area metric theories have been proposed as effective descriptions in a number of quantum gravity approaches: as continuum limit of effective spin foams, as an effective description for string theory and in the context of holography. Area metric actions allow for non-topological parity violating terms, which opens the possibility of observationally determining the Barbero-Immirzi parameter. We consider the shift symmetric version of linearized area metric theory in Lorentzian signature, which arises in particular from spin foams and modified Plebanski theory, and avoids ghost and tachyonic instabilities in the graviton sector. We discuss the gravitational wave like solutions of this theory and through an analysis of the coupling to electro-magnetism, deduce the signals in gravitational wave detectors. Using polarized light in such interferometers allows in principle to measure area metric induced birefringence. For the non-length excitations that accompany a gravitational wave this birefringence turns out to be independent of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter; the parameter is instead encoded in the polarization structure of the massive non-length waves, where it rotates the axes of the induced birefringence. Assuming Planck massive non-length excitations in the area metric the resulting signals are however extremely weak.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Dittrich

item.title: Target-space fusion of classical topological defects
item.description: arXiv:2608.21121v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical fusion of sigma-model defects is commonly approached by combining their worldsheet actions and eliminating the intermediate fields. This procedure, however, does not systematically identify the resulting target-space defect or its possible branches. We address this problem by formulating fusion as a reduction of the target-space defect data. Local descent of the intrinsic two-form and global descent of the connection determine the admissible branches. For symmetry-preserving bi-branes in the $SU(2)$ WZW model and Hopf-fibre T-duality defects, the prescription reproduces the known biconjugacy-class branches and the finite family of fibre-shift defects. The appearance of several branches provides a classical manifestation of non-invertible fusion. We further use the framework to construct TsT and T-dual biconjugacy defects, including their global consistency conditions. It therefore provides a systematic method for computing classical fusion and constructing new defects from known ones.
item.dc:creator: Saskia Demulder, Chuying Wang

item.title: Non-perturbative news from the conformal window
item.description: arXiv:2608.23674v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamical symmetry breaking plays a crucial role in mass and scale generation. In QCD-like theories, its dependence on the number of fermion flavours determines the phase structure and the transition to the conformal regime. In this work, we compute non-perturbative corrections relevant to this phenomenom, including momentum dependencies and field invariants essential for an adequate realisation of the global symmetries, by means of the functional renormalisation group and the generalised flow equation. We find that the critical gauge coupling required for dynamical chiral symmetry breaking acquires a strong dependence on the number of flavours and increases sharply at $N_f^\textrm{crit}\simeq 7.30$ for $N_c=3$. This establishes a new picture of the phase transition to the conformal window that disfavours Miransky/BKT scaling and walking regimes but supports a first-order quantum phase transition and a critical region with exotic dynamics and symmetric fermion mass gaps.
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Pastor-Guti\'errez

item.title: Color-Kinematics Duality and the Double Copy in Curved Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2608.23686v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. This review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. After recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in AdS, dS, and other non-trivial backgrounds. We then review classical and field-level maps, including Kerr--Schild, Weyl, Cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. A separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. Throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Carrillo Gonz\'alez

item.title: Bound States in Perturbative Quantum Gravity with Hydrogen-like Degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2608.29402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent results in the study of gravitational scattering amplitudes indicate that some highly-symmetric relativistic systems may exactly conserve a version of the Laplace-Runge-Lenz (LRL) vector in two-body bound states. We make a systematic study, in the context of a generic EFT of long-range interactions due to the exchange of massless mediator particles of spins 0, $\frac{1}{2}$, 1, $\frac{3}{2}$, 2, of the conditions for the conservation of a hidden LRL vector; both classically (no orbital precession) and quantum-mechanically (hydrogen-like degeneracy of bound states). The calculations require several new technical developments including the extension of relativistic post-Minkowskian potential matching to quantum corrections and the incorporation of long-range forces due to the exchange of pairs of massless fermions. We find that while classically the absence of precession is a generic property of a large class of models, including Kaluza-Klein theories, with vector and scalar exchanges, maintaining the degeneracy quantum-mechanically requires a surprising cancellation between gravitons and 6 Majorana gravitinos, hinting at a special role for $\mathcal{N}=6$ supergravity.
item.dc:creator: Callum R. T. Jones, Shruti Paranjape, Marcos Skowronek

item.title: ABJM/BMN Index Matching in the Plane-Wave Limit
item.description: arXiv:2609.07872v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish coefficientwise equality between the refined supersymmetric indices of ABJM theory and the BMN matrix model in the plane-wave limit at every fixed positive Chern-Simons level k. For multi-membrane families with fixed multiplicities, and hence fixed finite ABJM gauge rank, the equality holds as all longitudinal momenta tend to infinity with their pairwise differences fixed. Scalar-dressed equal-flux ABJM monopoles correspond to BMN vacua of fuzzy-sphere membranes: multiplicities count coincident membranes, whereas flux magnitudes give the momentum per membrane along the M-theory circle. At the index level, the associated Higgs residues yield a diagonal-holonomy integral for the ABJM plane-wave contribution, whose monopole-harmonic kernel agrees with the BMN matrix-harmonic kernel up to the finite BMN upper-spin cutoff. At finite momentum, the full index difference splits into the non-plane-wave remainder and the harmonic tail above this cutoff. Increasing k shifts the former to higher fugacity grade without changing the surviving kernel or the cutoff contribution. This gives a coefficientwise, multi-membrane extension of the earlier single-membrane index relation.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Ming Chang, Kangning Liu

item.title: Bogomol'nyi equations for Kruglov strings
item.description: arXiv:2609.08111v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct the Bogomol'nyi equations for Abelian gauge--Higgs vortices in which the Maxwell gauge sector is replaced by Kruglov nonlinear electrodynamics, a power-law family that interpolates between Maxwell theory, Born--Infeld electrodynamics, and exponential electrodynamics, characterized by a dimensionless exponent $\sigma$. Using the stressless method, we derive a pair of first-order equations directly from the vanishing of the spatial stress tensor, without assuming the Higgs potential \textit{a priori}. For generic $\sigma$, the gauge and Higgs sectors are coupled through an implicit algebraic relation. We therefore introduce a constitutive map $\Phi(Y;\sigma)$ and analyze its monotonicity and range to determine the conditions for a smooth admissible Bogomol'nyi branch. For $\sigma>1/2$, the constitutive map is strictly monotonic and unbounded, whereas for $0<\sigma<1/2$ it possesses a finite maximum; the marginal case $\sigma=1/2$ is bounded. These properties yield explicit bounds on the nonlinear parameter $\beta$ for the latter cases. We further obtain closed-form constitutive relations, BPS potentials, and gauge-field equations for six representative values of $\sigma$, spanning linear, quadratic, and cubic algebraic structures. The corresponding vortex profiles are then computed numerically. The resulting BPS string tension is purely topological, $\mu_{\rm BPS}=2\pi n$, independent of both $\sigma$ and $\beta$.
item.dc:creator: I. Praseyto, U. Ubaydillah, H. S. Ramadhan

item.title: Real-Time Instanton Dynamics in a Triple-Well to Double-Well Homotopy
item.description: arXiv:2609.10621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the singularities which the analytically continued double-well instanton develops in real (Minkowski) time are not an inherent feature of real-time tunneling solutions. Rather, they can be viewed as arising from a singular limit of a one-parameter family of regular real-time solutions. Using a linear homotopy between a triple-well and a double-well potential, we construct a family of potentials, parametrized by $p\in(0,1)$, whose real-time ($\alpha=0$) instanton solutions are everywhere regular and bounded. For any Wick rotation angle $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$, we prove that regularity is generic up to a measure-zero set. There exists a countably infinite, closed-form family of potential parameters $\{p^{\mathrm{singular}}_{k}(\alpha)\}_{k\geq0}$ at which the instanton becomes singular at exactly two points of the rotated time axis, never more. In the strict double-well limit, $p\to 1$ taken at $\alpha=0$, the entire family collapses onto the single point $(p,\alpha) = (1,0)$ at which the singular pairs of all $k$ occur simultaneously. This phenomenon produces the infinite singular comb found by Cherman and \"Unsal. By solving the complexified equations of motion in terms of Weierstrass elliptic functions, we trace this comb to classical imaginary turning points receding to $\pm\mathrm{i}\infty$, giving a unified geometric and algebraic account of when, and exactly how often, real-time instantons become singular. We further show that the action of the continued instanton is independent of $\alpha$ only in its real part: its imaginary part jumps by one real-time period action at each singular angle, the $\alpha$-independence found by Cherman and \"Unsal being the degenerate case of the double well, in which no such jump occurs.
item.dc:creator: Vojt\v{e}ch Loubal (Charles University), Tom\'a\v{s} S\'ykora (Charles University), \v{S}imon Kos (University of West Bohemia)

item.title: Two Recursions for the Seiberg-Witten Prepotential: Zamolodchikov's Recursion, the AGT Correspondence and Topological Recursion on the Seiberg-Witten Curve
item.description: arXiv:2609.12672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Seiberg-Witten prepotential of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory can be reached by two recursions of very different nature, and this thesis compares them explicitly. The first part is a self-contained review of the microscopic side: the ADHM construction as a hyperk\"ahler quotient, the supersymmetric measure on the instanton moduli space, Seiberg-Witten theory, and the one- and two-instanton contributions computed by non-commutative resolution and localisation. The second part introduces the $\Omega$-background and Nekrasov's partition function, and uses the AGT correspondence to turn Zamolodchikov's recursion for Virasoro conformal blocks into a recursion for the instanton partition function. For pure $SU(2)$, this recursion is run up to five instantons, including the first corrections in $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$. In the last part, the same quantities are obtained from the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion on the Seiberg-Witten curve, which yields the Taylor expansion of the prepotential around an arbitrary point of the Coulomb branch. For pure $SU(2)$ we give the Bergman kernel and the $B$-periods of $\omega_{0,3}$, $\omega_{0,4}$ and $\omega_{1,1}$ in closed form. They reproduce the instanton series generated by Zamolodchikov's recursion, remain valid at strong coupling, where they detect the massless monopole, and at genus one give the first correction to the self-dual $\Omega$-background. The two recursions are thus complementary: one is exact in the vacuum expectation value and perturbative in the instanton number, the other is exact in the instanton parameter and perturbative around a fixed vacuum. We formulate a conjecture relating the $B$-periods of $\omega_{g,n}$ to the derivatives of the genus-$g$ free energy, and list open problems.
item.dc:creator: Bastam Tajik

item.title: Integrable Chiral Quantum Field Theories with Spacetime-Dependent Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2609.13377v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a class of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories with interactions that depend on both space and time. The construction starts from a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix satisfying braiding unitarity and the Yang--Baxter equation. Each freely moving right- or left-moving particle carries a characteristic coordinate that remains constant along its trajectory, and the scattering matrix depends on differences of these coordinates. The many-body amplitudes form a discrete connection over the coordinate-ordering sectors. The Yang--Baxter equation gives local path independence, while periodic winding on a spatial circle produces quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (qKZ) difference equations expressing global flatness. Once a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints is specified, these transport equations determine the exact wavefunction in every fixed-particle-number sector. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics give couplings that depend on both space and time. For the chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization, we solve the qKZ equations for this full characteristic family using off-shell Bethe vectors. The resulting amplitudes are written in the characteristic labels, and their pullbacks give exact many-body wavefunctions for the corresponding space-time-dependent couplings. The two-body amplitude is a ratio of Gamma functions that resums the phase shifts from successive scattering processes. Equal-slope affine maps give a spatially homogeneous specialization in which the coupling depends only on time, and the Bethe ansatz with constant coupling is recovered when the qKZ step vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Pradip Kattel

item.title: Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.17195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Entropy is a 1-cocycle in information cohomology; we generalize this to the quantum setting via Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. For an inclusion of von Neumann algebras N contained in M with a faithful normal state w admitting a cyclic and separating vector, and a conditional expectation E: M -> N (whose existence is equivalent to modular invariance of N by Takesaki's theorem), we construct the entanglement complex as the image of the transgression map tau_w on the relative cyclic complex, where A is a dense *-subalgebra of M and B = A intersect N. Our main result identifies entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map HC*(A) -> HC*(B), up to the connecting homomorphism d of the long exact sequence of the pair (A,B); when d = 0, the identification is exact. The relative modular cocycle u_t = (Dw : D(w|_N) o E)_t generates explicit entanglement classes when E is not w-invariant, with the Araki relative entropy as its infinitesimal generator. The framework accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, and leads to a holographic proposal: a subspace of H^1_ent is conjecturally dual to linearized modular Hamiltonian perturbations of the bulk entanglement wedge. We verify the construction in finite-dimensional, type II_1, and type III_1 examples.
item.dc:creator: R. C. Rashkov

item.title: Gauge Origami of the Conifold $\times$ $\mathbb{C}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.23556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct gauge-origami systems on the toric Calabi--Yau fourfold $\mathcal{C}\times\mathbb{C}$ from its brane brick model. Brick matchings and phase boundaries determine elementary D6- and D4-brane framings, respectively, realizing the magnificent-four, tetrahedron-instanton, and spiked-instanton sectors in a unified framed quiver quantum mechanics. We define their partition functions by Jeffrey--Kirwan residues and describe the fixed points in terms of colored BPS crystals. General gauge-origami configurations are obtained by combining these elementary sectors through their common fractional D0-brane quiver. This construction provides a first step toward gauge origami on general toric Calabi--Yau fourfolds.
item.dc:creator: Taro Kimura, Go Noshita

item.title: Exact Color Kinematics Duality in the Cosmological Correlators
item.description: arXiv:2609.28639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study color kinematics duality and related double-copy and BCJ structures in the cosmological Grassmannian framework. The simplicity of these correlators in this framework makes it possible to test the double copy construction beyond flat space. We show that the four-point gluon correlator admits a representation whose kinematic numerators satisfy an algebraically exact Jacobi identity, $n_s$ + $n_t$ + $n_u$ = 0. Replacing color factors with kinematic numerators gives a graviton correlator that reproduces the correct factorization residues and flat-space limit, which matches with the BCFW result up to terms regular in all exchange channels. In addition, we construct a differential bi-adjoint scalar matrix whose null vector gives rise to a differential BCJ relation among color-ordered gluon correlators. We further explore an s-copy construction for general integer-spin correlators and show that for odd spin the corresponding numerators satisfy a Jacobi identity. Finally, we develop a differential representation for scalar four-point correlators with gluon exchange. These results establish algebraic and differential aspects of graviton and gluon correlators in curved spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Aswini Bala, Sachin Jain, Vibhor Singh

item.title: All-Plus QED Wavefunctions in de Sitter Space
item.description: arXiv:2609.29356v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a compact all-multiplicity formula for tree-level late-time wavefunction coefficients of scalar QED in four-dimensional de Sitter space, with a conformally coupled charged scalar pair and positive-helicity photons. The result admits both a recursive representation in terms of shifted lower-point coefficients and an explicit finite sum involving only kinematic factors. The flat-space amplitudes vanish for two or more photons, yet the de Sitter coefficients remain nonzero. These zeros enforce cancellations of the total-energy residue and, through factorization, of proper partial-energy residues involving multi-photon subamplitudes. Using a common-reference construction, we derive an exact lower-point recursion from Abelian Ward identities. Conformal symmetry provides an independent check: the partition sum solves the inhomogeneous Ward identity, while the total-energy term is a homogeneous solution. We also outline an analogous recursion in massless fermionic QED.
item.dc:creator: Song He, Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo

item.title: Genuine Multi-Entropy of Fully Symmetric Gaussian States
item.description: arXiv:2609.30754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the tri-partite genuine R\'enyi multi-entropy of fully symmetric Gaussian states as a function of the squeezing parameter for different total number of bosonic modes under different subsystem configurations. Exact results for a few modes are obtained, and we conjecture an asymptotic formula at the limit of large squeezing parameter as a function of the replica index $n$, while also finding subleading subsystem-size dependent terms for $n=3$ under a specific tripartition. We analytically show that the genuine $n=2$ R\'enyi multi-entropy of any pure bosonic Gaussian states is zero for any number of modes and for any tripartition. Furthermore, to investigate the dependence on subsystem size, we plot the curve of genuine R\'enyi multi-entropy as a function of the number of modes in the subsystems while keeping the total number of modes fixed. We discuss differences and similarities between this result and studies of the multi-entropy curve for Haar random states. In particular, we identify a subsystem size configuration related with the multi-entropy time in an evaporating black hole for which the behavior of the genuine multi-entropy changes.
item.dc:creator: Hugo A. Camargo, Mitsuhiro Nishida

item.title: Symmetry-Restoring Counter-terms in Massive Gauge Theories with Non-Anticommuting $\gamma_5$ via Gauge-Invariant Sector Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2609.38557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the one-loop breaking of the Slavnov-Taylor (ST) identities in a massive Abelian chiral gauge theory with spontaneous symmetry breaking, regularized in the Breitenlohner-Maison-`t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. We also provide the one-loop finite counter-terms required to restore the one-loop ST identities. The recent formulation of spontaneously broken models based on the Fr\"ohlich-Morchio-Strocchi (FMS) gauge-invariant and dynamical (i.e. propagating inside loops) fields is used. The proposed algebraic approach holds true to all orders in the loop expansion and allows for a consistent decomposition of the ST breaking into independent sectors. By using cohomological techniques we eventually constrain the dependence of the ST breaking on the vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field. This yields a set of differential equations that provide a useful check of the mass-dependent terms in the ST breaking terms in the broken phase. They can be generalized to the non-Abelian case, both in the gauge-invariant formalism and in the conventional one. In the massless limit we find agreement with previous calculations present in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Quadri

item.title: Large gaps and BTZ entropy in modular spectra with positive integer degeneracies
item.description: arXiv:2609.39930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct modular-invariant torus partition functions with a unique vacuum, discrete energy levels and positive integer degeneracies by recursively repairing the Maloney--Witten--Keller modular completion of the Virasoro vacuum. Exact modular repairs and finite moment matching discretize successive spectral bands while preserving earlier levels and controlling convergence. For $c_L=c_R=c$ and $a=(c-1)/12$, the construction realizes primary dimension gaps $\Delta_1=(1+\kappa)a$ for sufficiently small fixed $\kappa>0$, and $\Delta_1=a+\delta$ for any fixed $\delta\ge0$, at every sufficiently large real $c$. Every nonvacuum primary satisfies $h,\bar h\ge(c-1)/24$. In the fixed-$\delta$ family, spectra can be chosen whose densities of states, smoothed with a fixed nonnegative normalized smooth kernel of compact support, match the correspondingly smoothed prediction of a single perturbative BTZ saddle through every fixed finite order in $1/c$. The count includes all spins and Virasoro descendants. Its logarithm reproduces the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy and its corrections at every fixed positive $E/c$, where $E=\Delta-c/12$. This includes $0<E<c/12$, where thermal AdS dominates the canonical ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Ming Chang, Reiko Liu, Wen-Jie Ma

item.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.00516v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal. Two characterizations of these duals exist in the literature: a modular one, based on mock modularity with a prescribed shadow, and a resurgent one, based on Borel--Mordell integrals and transseries. We prove that the two characterizations are equivalent. We construct a new family of dual false theta functions for values of positive integer $p$ satisfying a Pell-equation condition. Its members are built from Zwegers' indefinite theta functions, have integer coefficients, and have effective central charge $c_{\text{eff}} \leq 1$. We also show that the mock theta functions of Li and Schwagenscheidt satisfy these characterizations and arise from a natural regularization of the divergent product $\eta^{3}(\tau)\psi_{p, a}(- \tau)$.
item.dc:creator: Mrunmay Jagadale

item.title: Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet quintessential inflation: From super-inflation to emergent warm inflation
item.description: arXiv:2610.01665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents a unified inflationary and late-time cosmology, developed within Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity coupled to three scalar fields, governed by a single potential and coupling function throughout cosmic history. Permitting the Gauss-Bonnet coupling to depend on the field content, rather than assigning it arbitrarily, produces a two-phase inflationary scenario: the higher-curvature term initially drives expansion and later becomes a subdominant. The initial super-inflationary stage ends dynamically when the geometrically induced stabilization of the waterfall field fails, at a field value determined by the combination $(n-1)Q$. Coherent oscillations of the waterfall condensate serve as the initial radiation source, replacing conventional reheating and establishing the thermal bath necessary for the subsequent warm phase. Utilizing a two-stage dissipation mechanism with $\Gamma_\phi\propto T^3$, the scalar and tensor spectra are derived while retaining Gauss-Bonnet contributions, demonstrating that the growth of inflaton fluctuations is regulated by the shear viscosity of the bath, which is essential for model viability. A quartic potential, previously excluded in the cold scenario, becomes viable, with $n_s$ within the Planck $1\sigma$ band and $r$ suppressed. Agreement with the spectral index is generic, while internal consistency confines the model to a narrow band in $(n-1)Q$. Finally, the release of the third scalar near matter-radiation equality transforms a very small mass scale into a very large coupling by a logic inverse to the seesaw mechanism. At late times, the inflaton persists as dark energy.
item.dc:creator: Omar Chahboun, Rachid Ahl Laamara, El Hassan Saidi

item.title: Quantum Gravity from Gluing Consistency: AdS/CFT to Spin-Foams
item.description: arXiv:2610.03652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We argue that BF theory with $SO(d+1,1)$ gauge group provides a SymTFT ''skeleton'' for building AdS$_{d+1}$/CFT$_d$ pairs via gluing consistency as the bootstrap principle, loosely analogous to how compact Chern-Simons theory is a TQFT skeleton for rational CFTs. This is a non-perturbative $bulk$ framework for quantum gravity. The bootstrap is formulated as presentation independence of physical amplitudes within a universal, defect-closed BF sewing calculus, which includes Wilson lines, codimension-two monodromy defects, and their junctions. The flat BF connection encodes the conformal geometry of the boundary, while Wilson-line path integrals construct candidate quantum-gravity microstates and charge sectors. When the bootstrapped spectrum has a stress tensor, Ward identities naturally connect it to the $B$-field, a relation we call generalized simplicity. In large-$N$, large-gap regimes admitting a gravitational EFT, this motivates the introduction of an effective notion of the $B$-field. In the Einstein limit, this becomes the ''simplicity'' relation used in spin-foam models. Conventional spin-foam models try to obtain gravity by constraining BF theory. We suggest instead that BF theory is the Platonic sewing skeleton, from which theories are to be bootstrapped. Despite the topological nature of the skeleton, perturbative local bulk fields can emerge via Wilson-towers of multi-trace primaries, reproducing their one-loop determinants. We note that the BF Fourier kernel is a suggestive higher-dimensional analogue of the modular-$S$ structure. Because the bulk gluing principle in itself does not require a boundary description, the framework is conceptually broader than AdS/CFT. We sketch how de Sitter space may fit into this picture, with a natural role for observers. Our approach elevates gluing consistency to a universal bulk principle underlying theories of quantum gravity.
item.dc:creator: Chethan Krishnan

item.title: QCD_2: 't Hooft equation vs. relativistic Schroedinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.08673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss 2-dimensional $QCD$ with a fundamental quark of mass $m$ in the 't Hooft limit ($N \to \infty, \, g^2 \to 0, \, g^2N =$ const). The spectrum of this theory includes a chain of meson states. The masses of these states can be evaluated by solving the proper integral Bethe-Salpeter equation. An alternative simple procedure consists in solving the Schr\"odinger equation for the relativistic Hamiltonian $$ \hat H\ =\ 2\sqrt{\hat p^2 + m^2} + \sigma |x| $$ with the string tension $\sigma = g^2N/4$. We compare the results obtained by these two methods. In the leading semiclassical approximation, they coincide. We show, however, that the preasymptotic WKB corrections to the masses calculated in these two ways are different. For the ground state, they play an essential role. But already for $n=3$, the relative difference between the two predictions does not exceed 2.5\% and rapidly falls off as $n$ increases.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Smilga

item.title: Maximally symmetric black holes with torsion in Lovelock gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.10348v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the existence of static black hole solutions with maximally symmetric horizons and nontrivial torsion in five-dimensional Lovelock gravity. For each symmetry class, we obtain a black hole solution characterized by two independent constants. We also determine the conserved charges associated with these solutions.
item.dc:creator: B. Cvetkovi\'c, D. Simi\'c

item.title: Null string holography in AdS from local BRST descent
item.description: arXiv:2610.10540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the radial sector of a Carroll-Weyl gauged null string in Poincar\'e $\mathrm{AdS}_D$ is locally trivial in BRST cohomology. In a quotient-adapted BFV basis, the radial coordinate, its conjugate momentum, and the associated ghosts form a contractible quartet. An explicit contracting homotopy extends this reduction to the full algebra of local spatial jets, leaving precisely the $(D-1)$-dimensional ILST BRST complex. The same quartet carries zero net Virasoro central charge, so that the anomaly condition of the parent theory, $D=27$, descends to the ILST condition $d=26$.
item.dc:creator: Sarthak Duary, Sourav Maji

item.title: Carroll-Weyl gauged null strings in AdS
item.description: arXiv:2610.10717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Carroll-Weyl gauged null string in the Poincar\'e patch of $\mathrm{AdS}_D$ and its BRST quantization. In Poincar\'e coordinates $X^A=(z,x^i)$, the radial conformal Killing vector $K=\partial_z$ becomes homothetic in a suitable conformally related frame. A field-dependent rescaling of the homothetic Hamiltonian constraint then leads to the radial-adapted basis $\mathcal{M}=\frac{1}{2}(P_z^2+P_iP^i)$, $\mathcal{L}=-P_AX'^A$, and $\mathcal{S}=P_z$, with $\mathcal{M}$ invariant along the Carroll-Weyl radial flow. Their modes form a $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ algebra extended by an abelian weight-one current. We classify the central extensions allowed by this residual algebra and find four independent cohomology classes in the $LL$, $LM$, $LS$, and $SS$ channels. We then construct the associated BRST complex, including the ghost pair for the radial Carroll-Weyl constraint. In the canonical highest-weight first-order representation, only the Virasoro-type central extension is realized: $(c_{LL},c_{LM},c_{LS},c_{SS})=(2D-54,0,0,0)$. Cancellation of the corresponding nontrivial BRST cocycle therefore gives $D=27$ in this representation. This differs structurally from the minimal flat Carroll-Weyl theory, where the dilation constraint $X\cdot P$ gives extra anomaly channels.
item.dc:creator: Sarthak Duary, Sourav Maji

item.title: Triggering Higgs vacuum decay
item.description: arXiv:2301.03620v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Standard Model Higgs potential seems unstable at field values $h > h_{\rm top} \sim 10^{10}$ GeV. Vacuum decay can be triggered by $N\sim 4\pi/\lambda \sim 1000$ overlapped Higgs bosons with energy $\sqrt{\lambda} h_{\rm top}$. However, this configuration is stimulated by ultra-high energy collisions with a $\exp(-{\cal O}(N))$ suppression, comparable to spontaneous vacuum decay: no `Higgspolosion' enhancement arises. This implies that ultra-high energy cosmic ray collisions are safe, despite that their number (in production sites) likely is tens of orders of magnitude higher than what usually estimated (in space). We speculate on how vacuum decay could be induced classically at futuristic ultra-high energy colliders (either using a few right-handed electron beams, or a double collision producing an in-coming wave of $N$ boosted Higgs bosons) and on how the resulting vacuum bubble could be controlled to extract energy.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Strumia

item.title: Regularized interacting scalar quantum field theories
item.description: arXiv:2502.14117v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we consider self-interacting scalar quantum field theories over a $d$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with various interaction Lagrangians which are suitable functions of the field. The interacting field observables are represented as power series over the free theory by means of perturbation theory. The object which is employed to obtain this power series is the time-ordered exponential of the interaction Lagrangian which is the $S$-matrix of the theory and thus itself a power series in the coupling constant of the theory. We analyze a regularization procedure which makes the $S$-matrix convergent to well-defined unitary operators. This regularization depends on two parameters. One describes how much the high-frequency contributions in the propagators are tamed and a second one describes how much the large-field contributions are suppressed in the interaction Lagrangian. We finally discuss the limits in which the parameters are removed in some lower-dimensional theories and for specific interaction Lagrangians. In particular, we show, by an abstract argument, that in three spacetime dimensions for a $\phi^4_3$ theory one obtains sequences of unitary operators which are weakly-$*$ convergent to bounded operators in the limit of vanishing parameters. Although we lose control over the unitarity of the operator obtained in the limit and although the uniqueness of the limit is not under control, we notice that some basic causal properties are satisfied by the corresponding interacting fields. We furthermore observe that the very same limits, applied at fixed order, give back the ordinary perturbation theory results. Finally, we discuss a possible extension of these results to the case of a $\phi^4_4$ theory.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Pinamonti

item.title: On Ising model in magnetic field on the lattice
item.description: arXiv:2504.18744v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the free energy of the classical square-lattice Ising model in a uniform real magnetic field $h$, for which no exact solution is known. We first conjecture a closed-form expression built from the one-dimensional Ising chain and Onsager's hypergeometric solution. Comparing with high-precision tensor renormalization group (TRG) data, we find that it deviates by up to $2.6\%$, has no spontaneous magnetization, and gives an effective critical-isotherm exponent $\delta \to 1$. However, using the Lee--Yang circle theorem, we show that the exact free energy is a superposition of one-dimensional Ising chains in the same field, weighted by a temperature-dependent (normalized, but not always positive) distribution of squared Lee--Yang gaps, of which our first expression is a single-chain approximation. Exact results (Onsager, Yang, the strong-field expansion and the Lee--Yang solution at $\beta h = i\pi/2$) become sum rules for this distribution. We propose a simple form for it, fixed by Onsager's free energy and the exact strong-field limit without any fit to numerical data. This \emph{improved} conjecture agrees with TRG to $0.15\%$ for all $\beta$ and $h$, reproduces Yang's spontaneous magnetization exactly, has a positive specific heat, and yields the critical isotherm $M\propto h^{1/\delta}$ with $\delta = 15.2$ and amplitude $1.055$, compared with the exact $\delta=15$ and $1.059$. A refined form, which builds in additional input from Ising field theory (including the exact critical isotherm, $\delta=15$) and a few constants adjusted to transfer-matrix and TRG data, matches the TRG free energy to $4\times 10^{-5}$.
item.dc:creator: Raghav G. Jha

item.title: Reassessing the foundations of Metric-Affine Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2505.05349v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reassess foundational aspects of Metric-Affine Gravity (MAG) in light of the Dressing Field Method, a tool allowing to systematically build gauge-invariant field variables. To get MAG started, one has to deal with the problem of "gauge translations". We first recall that Cartan geometry is the proper mathematical foundation for gauge theories of gravity, and that this problem never arises in that framework, which still allows to clarify the geometric status of gauge translations. Then, we show how the MAG kinematics is obtained via dressing in a technically streamlined way, which highlights that it reduces to a Cartan-geometric kinematics.
item.dc:creator: J. Fran\c{c}ois, L. Ravera

item.title: Large condensation in enriched $\infty$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2506.23632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate that many algebraic features of higher condensation theory are really features of higher algebra. We work in the context of monads on the unit of a monoidal 2- category. Assuming that 2-categorical unstraightening is monoidal, we show that the functor which takes such a monad to its Eilenberg-Moore object is lax monoidal. We use this to introduce an analog of condensation for codimension-i symmetries, without assuming dualizability. We give sufficient conditions for Morita equivalence of endomorphisms of condensates. We relate higher centralizers to iterated categories of modules. Along the way, we prove results pertaining to functoriality of Day convolution for enriched infinity-categories, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Devon Stockall

item.title: Conifold gap and all-genus mirror symmetry for local $\mathbb{P}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2509.19298v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Conifold Gap Conjecture asserts that the polar part of the Gromov-Witten potential of a Calabi-Yau threefold near its conifold locus has a universal expression described by the logarithm of the Barnes $G$-function. In this paper, I prove the Conifold Gap Conjecture for the local projective plane. The proof relates the higher genus conifold Gromov-Witten generating series of local $\mathbb{P}^2$ to the thermodynamics of a certain statistical mechanical ensemble of repulsive particles on the positive half-line. As a corollary, this establishes the all-genus mirror principle for local $\mathbb{P}^2$ through the direct integration of the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equations.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Brini

item.title: Collective Properties of Gravitational Perturbations in Thermal Environments on a Dynamical Background
item.description: arXiv:2510.22346v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A thermal plasma dresses soft gauge fields, turning them into collective modes with a plasmon gap and Landau damping. In this paper, we ask whether a thermal radiation plasma does the same to gravitational perturbations. For gravity, the thermal soft scale coincides with the Hubble rate. Any such gap therefore lies at the horizon scale, where the expansion of the background cannot be neglected. We model radiation by a conformal scalar and compute its linear response to metric perturbations directly on a flat FLRW background. We test this response against the diffeomorphism Ward identities. The adiabatic dispersion relation yields a gapped collective mode with $\omega_p^2 = 8\mathcal{H}^2/5$, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the conformal Hubble rate. The imaginary part of its frequency, however, is dominated by the background expansion and does not represent Landau damping. In the radiation background, the tensor modes obey a real-time integro-differential equation that reproduces Weinberg's damping of gravitational waves. The initial-time boundary of the retarded response keeps superhorizon modes frozen until horizon reentry despite the gap. The superhorizon growth found in earlier analyses arises from discarding the memory of the retarded response and from a local-equilibrium state prescription that violates the Ward identities. More generally, the Ward identities forbid any local state response beyond the collisionless kernel.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhisa Ota

item.title: The poltergeist mechanism - Enhancement of scalar-induced gravitational waves with early matter-dominated era -
item.description: arXiv:2511.07266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gravitational waves induced by primordial density perturbations provide a powerful probe of the Universe's thermal history, which may include an early matter-dominated (eMD) era predicted by well-motivated particle-physics models. The induced GWs can be significantly enhanced when the Universe undergoes a sudden transition from an eMD era to an era with pressure, such as a radiation or kination era. This enhancement arises from the growth of density perturbations during the eMD era and their rapid oscillations during the era with pressure. This phenomenon is called the poltergeist mechanism. In this review, we explain the essence of the poltergeist mechanism and explore concrete scenarios in which such an enhancement can occur.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Inomata, Kazunori Kohri, Takahiro Terada

item.title: Generalized Beth--Uhlenbeck entropy formula from the $\Phi-$derivable approach
item.description: arXiv:2512.03876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a generalized Beth-Uhlenbeck formula for the entropy of a dense fermion system with strong two-particle correlations, including scattering states and bound states. We work within the $\Phi-$derivable approach to the thermodynamic potential. The formula takes the form of an energy-momentum integral over a statistical distribution function times a unique spectral density. In the near mass-shell limit, the spectral density reduces, contrary to na\"{i}ve expectations, not to a Lorentzian but rather to a "squared Lorentzian" shape. The relation of the Beth-Uhlenbeck formula to the $\Phi$-derivable approach is exact at the two-loop level for $\Phi$. The formalism we develop, which extends the Beth-Uhlenbeck approach beyond the low-density limit, includes Mott dissociation of bound states, in accordance with Levinson's theorem, and the self-consistent back reaction of correlations in the fermion propagation. We discuss applications to further systems, such as quark matter and nuclear matter.
item.dc:creator: David Blaschke, Gerd R\"opke, Gordon Baym

item.title: Finite-size clocks in quantum field theory and the twin paradox
item.description: arXiv:2512.06076v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory impose fundamental limitations on our ability to measure time at arbitrarily short scales. To investigate the impact of universal quantum field theory effects on observer-dependent time measurements, we introduce a clock model based on the vacuum decay probability of a finite-sized quantum system. This model defines an effective notion of proper time that depends on the microscopic properties of the clock and on how it samples vacuum fluctuations along its trajectory. We show that, in the long-time regime, this notion of time reduces to the usual proper time of special relativity. However, by studying a microscopic twin-paradox scenario, we find that, in general, time is not determined solely by the trajectory connecting two events, but also by how vacuum fluctuations interact with the internal structure of the clocks.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. H. Zambianco and T. R. Perche, Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043003 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Matheus H. Zambianco, T. Rick Perche

item.title: Geometric Quantum Computation
item.description: arXiv:2512.09640v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a new model of quantum computation rooted in the representation theory of the mass less sector of unitary irreducible representations of the extended Poincare group developed in [1].
item.dc:creator: Marco Zaopo

item.title: The Arf-Brown-Kervaire invariant on a lattice
item.description: arXiv:2512.11424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a lattice formulation of the Arf-Brown-Kervaire (ABK) invariant which takes values in $\mathbb{Z}_8$. Compared to the standard $\mathbb{Z}$-valued index, the ABK invariant is more involved in that it arises in Majorana fermion partition functions with reflection symmetry on two-dimensional non-orientable manifolds, and its definition contains an infinite sum over Dirac eigenvalues that requires proper regularization. We employ the massive Wilson Dirac operator, with and without domain-walls, on standard two-dimensional square lattices, and use its Pfaffian for the definition. Twisted boundary conditions and cross-caps, which reverse the orientation, are introduced to realize nontrivial topologies equipped with nontrivial $\mathrm{Pin}^{-}$ structures of Majorana fermions. We verify numerically (and partly analytically) that our formulation on a torus, Klein bottle, real projective plane (as well as its triple connected sum), and two types of M\"obius strip reproduces the known values in continuum theory.
item.dc:creator: Sho Araki, Hidenori Fukaya, Tetsuya Onogi, Satoshi Yamaguchi

item.title: Symmetric Mass Generation as a Multicritical Point with Enhanced Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2512.24836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore the phase diagram of a lattice fermion model that exhibits three distinct phases: a massless fermion phase, a massive fermion phase with spontaneous symmetry breaking induced by a fermion bilinear condensate, and a massive fermion phase with symmetric mass generation. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method on large cubical lattices, we find evidence for traditional second-order critical points separating the first two and the latter two phases. Remarkably, these critical points appear to merge at a multicritical point with enhanced symmetry when the symmetry breaking parameter is tuned to zero, giving rise to the recently discovered direct second-order transition between the massless and symmetric massive fermion phases.
item.dc:creator: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic

item.title: Geometry-Induced Skin Effect in Electron Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.17229v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In ultra-clean 2d materials electron viscosity is as important as Ohmic dissipation and electron transport exhibits hydrodynamic features. Using a simple framework of Brinkman equations we find that hydrodynamic electron flows give rise to a geometric skin effect: sharp obstacles locally enhance the current suppressing it far from the edges where the flow is unobstructed. This effect arises within hydrodynamic transport with finite momentum relaxation and does not rely on ballistic dynamics. Our results provide a natural hydrodynamic interpretation of edge-enhanced and double-bump current profiles observed in constricted geometries. By comparing with recent scanning NV magnetometry experiments on gated graphene, we demonstrate that such flow patterns are consistent with viscous hydrodynamics shaped by geometry, clarifying the role of geometric effects in the interpretation of electronic flow experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Paw{\l}owski, Piotr Sur\'owka, Konstantin Zarembo

item.title: Many-body effects on dense matter with hyperons at finite temperature
item.description: arXiv:2602.06815v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we present the first extension of the Many-Body Forces (MBF) Model to finite temperature. The MBF Model describes nuclear matter in a relativistic quantum hadrodynamics formalism that takes many-body forces into account through a field dependence of the nuclear interaction coupling constants. Assuming nuclear matter to be charge neutral, beta-equilibrated, and populated by the baryon octet, electrons, muons, and neutrinos, we explore the parameter of the model that controls many-body forces, three different hyperon coupling schemes (also introduced here for the first time in the MBF Model), and temperature effects to describe basic properties of nuclear matter, including the speed of sound, compressibility, and adiabatic index. We also investigate the mass-radius relation of neutron and protoneutron stars by solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations at zero and finite temperature, including scenarios with fixed entropy per baryon and lepton fraction. We find that different hyperon coupling schemes soften the equation of state to different degrees, requiring different degrees of many-body force effects to reproduce observations, although they are never zero. Multidimensional tables with our results are available in the CompOSE repository, ready to be used in astrophysical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Rafael B\'an Jacobsen, Ricardo Luciano Sonego Farias, Veronica Dexheimer

item.title: Phase diagram of a lattice fermion model with symmetric mass generation
item.description: arXiv:2602.18360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the phase structure of a model containing two flavors of massless staggered fermions interacting through two independent four-fermion couplings, UI and UB, formulated on a three-dimensional Euclidean space-time lattice. At UB = 0, this model is known to exhibit a direct second-order quantum phase transition between a massless fermion (MF) phase and a phase in which fermions acquire masses through the mechanism commonly referred to as symmetric mass generation (SMG). We demonstrate that introducing a small nonzero value of UB qualitatively alters this structure: the single exotic transition at UB = 0 splits into two distinct, conventional transitions, separated by an intermediate phase in which fermion masses arise through the standard mechanism of spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB). The first of these is a Gross-Neveu transition separating the MF phase from the SSB-induced massive phase, while the second is a three-dimensional XY transition between the SSB phase and the SMG phase. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method, we verify that the critical exponents associated with both transitions are consistent with the literature, thereby yielding a quantitative characterization of the resulting phase structure of the model.
item.dc:creator: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic

item.title: Looking for non-gaussianity in Pulsar Timing Arrays through the four point correlator
item.description: arXiv:2603.12311v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pulsar Timing Arrays have recently reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. In standard analyses, it is modeled through pulsar-dependent Fourier coefficients assumed to follow gaussian statistics, so that the signal is fully characterized by its two-point function. However, if the background arises from a finite population of inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries, non-gaussian features may emerge, making the determination of higher-order correlators essential. In this work, we compute the complete four-point correlator of the stochastic gravitational wave background Fourier coefficients for four arbitrary pulsar positions, identifying it as the leading probe of non-gaussianity. The result separates into a gaussian contribution, proportional to the square of the two-point function, and a genuinely non-gaussian connected component, whose non-trivial angular dependence generalizes the Hellings and Downs correlation to four pulsars. This angular structure depends only on averages of products of antenna pattern functions, and is therefore expected to be independent of the specific physical origin of the background. We further propose to incorporate the four-point correlator into the parameter-estimation pipeline by deriving a marginalized likelihood that perturbatively accounts for non-gaussian effects. Our results provide the theoretical framework to search for non-gaussian features in pulsar timing array data, opening the way to a more complete characterization of gravitational-wave backgrounds.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Kuntz, Clemente Smarra, Massimo Vaglio

item.title: Transverse force tomography inside a proton from Basis Light-front Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2603.25548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The twist-3 transverse spin--dependent nucleon structure function $g_2$ arises in high-energy processes involving a transversely polarized nucleon. Its connection to quark--gluon correlations allows for an interpretation in terms of the average transverse color Lorentz force acting on unpolarized quarks inside a transversely polarized nucleon. In this work, we investigate this force using light-front wave functions obtained by diagonalizing the light-front Hamiltonian with quantum chromodynamics inputs within the Basis Light-front Quantization approach. We evolve our results to a common scale of $5~\mathrm{GeV}^2$ and present the corresponding form factors in momentum space as well as the transverse force components in impact-parameter space. These distributions provide a complementary perspective on the Sivers asymmetry in transversely polarized deep-inelastic scattering. In the forward limit, we extract the twist-3 reduced matrix element $d_2$, and our results are found to be comparable with those from other theoretical calculations and experimental determinations.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Zhang, Chandan Mondal, Siqi Xu, Xingbo Zhao, James P. Vary

item.title: Entanglement in the $\theta$-vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2603.29287v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $\theta$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $\theta=\pi$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $\theta=\pi$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $\theta=\pi$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Grieninger, Dmitri E. Kharzeev, Eliana Marroquin

item.title: Matching Tidal Deformability (Wilson) Coefficients to Black Hole Love Numbers in Higher-Curvature Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2604.04259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a consistent mapping between tidal deformability coefficients (tidal Love numbers) and Wilson coefficients in effective field theory (EFT) descriptions of higher-curvature theories of gravity. In this work, we focus on the connection between the static response of a non-spinning black hole and the corresponding Wilson coefficient governing tidal imprints in gravitational-wave signals. We analyze a set of control cases to identify the key ingredients required for a systematic computation and matching procedure. In doing so, we highlight shortcomings in existing results that rely on the standard matching approach used in General Relativity when applied to higher-curvature gravity theories. As an explicit demonstration, we compute the relevant coefficients for cubic gravity theories.
